scopeReview: IMP-1.C: geographic information used in decision-making by governments, organizations and individuals. Applications include service access, hazard screening, routing, community information, temporal relevance and decision scales. No third-party questions or real-country statistics.
varietyReview: Four decision/evidence stimuli plus seven distinct applied scenarios; explicit objectives prevent several plausible policies from becoming competing correct answers. All five skills and all four key positions represented.
repetitionReview: No duplicated stem or numeric-only clone. Distinct decisions: constrained access, point-in-polygon hazard exposure, absolute population change, causal comparison and seven information-use limitations. Prior data-collection questions are not reworded as new methods-identification questions.

questions.independentReview: Independently filtered costs <=100, leaving R,T,U, and ranked their newly served populations 3000,2500,2000. The correct site is unique; no assumption of maximizing residents per cost was substituted.

questions.correctOption: School B is the mapped floodplain priority, even though School A enrolls more students.
questions.independentReview: Checked point-in-polygon positions independently: floodplain x=35..65; A.x=20, B.x=50, C.x=80. Only B is inside. No real hazard probability, causal claim or precise inundation depth is inferred.

questions.correctOption: Area A added the greatest number of residents.
questions.independentReview: Independently subtracted old from new counts: A2000, B1000, C200. Separately computed relative changes .5,1,.1 to rule out denominator confusion.

questions.correctOption: Both districts cooled equally; these data alone do not isolate the policy effect.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed changes 31−34=−3 and29−32=−3; difference in changes=0. A finite observational comparison cannot prove a zero causal effect or complete attribution.

questions.correctOption: Compare customer locations with the currently usable road network.
questions.independentReview: Separated the spatial decision from data acquisition. The combination supplies destinations plus traversable edges; it does not promise globally optimal or permanently valid routes.

questions.correctOption: The earlier count may omit newer settlement and service needs.
questions.independentReview: Checked temporal support: past accuracy and current relevance are different. Supplementation is warranted by changed settlement, not by an unsupported claim that all official data are unreliable.

questions.correctOption: Compare underlying values, dates and class breaks before inferring change.
questions.independentReview: Held the data constant while allowing thresholds to vary. The counterexample proves that changing appearance is insufficient evidence of a changed geographic condition.

questions.correctOption: Aggregate patterns can locate a potential audience without determining individual preferences.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished a probabilistic targeting aid from individual-level determinism, without assigning preferences to a real demographic group or claiming an actual business result.

questions.correctOption: Regional corridor patterns and local walking connections require different spatial detail.
questions.independentReview: Independently matched decision extent to useful evidence: intercity network versus immediate pedestrian connectivity. No claim that the larger-extent map necessarily has a larger representative fraction is made.

questions.correctOption: Compare probability estimates with exposure, vulnerability and current observations.
questions.independentReview: Separated hazard probability, exposed assets and vulnerability. The correct use does not invent numerical risk totals or equate a model estimate with a certain future event.

questions.correctOption: Validated community information can reveal spatial connections missing from official records.
questions.independentReview: Considered the documented mismatch in feature coverage, not an assumption that official or volunteered records are always correct. Verification can reconcile different collection purposes.
